lesson_title: One Taxi Ride Through Every Urban Zone
hook_text: One taxi ride crosses every zone in your Geography exam. Get in.
clip_script: Downtown, where you start, the buildings are tallest and the streets are fullest — banks, head offices, big stores stacked on the most expensive ground in the city. Why tall? Think of it as a tug-of-war over land: everyone wants the most reachable spot, the place all the taxis and trains converge, so the ground there costs a fortune, and the only way to afford a fortune is to stack thirty floors of rent on top of it. That is the CBD: dearest land, tallest buildings, busiest days — and quiet nights, because almost nobody sleeps there.
visual_style: Dashboard view rolling from a glass tower skyline through a scruffy transition ring, out past suburbs and townships to a highway mall node, zone labels sliding past like street signs.
pacing: Rolling momentum, one zone per beat, ending at the city's edge.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and name any zone from its description before the sentence ends.
